comments.body: From the Codex critique, 2026-10-24 (an inference from Apple's docs, not probed natively): UNTextInputNotificationAction takes a placeholder, not an editable initial value, so a banner cannot fill its reply field with a picked answer the way the conversation does. Option: one text-input action per offered answer, carrying the option in the action's identity, with the typed text as an optional note. Otherwise picking in a banner opens the conversation with the answer selected. Settle with a native probe before promising the banner behaves like the conversation.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Most questions agents put to the human are a choice between two or three things. Agreed in the Lectern page muster-group-conversation (2026-10-24): a post carries answers the agent offers (something like msg post --option "Run it now" --option "Skip it"; the spelling is open). The conversation view draws them as buttons, and the banner can offer them as its actions. Picking one fills the human's reply rather than sending it, so a note can go with it, and writing without picking stays an ordinary reply. The reply carries the choice twice: as text at the top of its body, which an agent reads with no new parsing, and as a field naming the question and the option, so Muster can show the question as answered. Digits must not pick an answer inside the message box, since a reply may start with "1.". Open: whether a question may take several answers, as Claude Code's multi-select does. Needs a field on a message, so a daemon protocol minor.
title: An agent can offer answers to a question it posts
